design: Replicate-holdout, non-circular. Replicate r3 of every (beta, a) cell is HELD OUT and never used in identification; replicates r1+r2 form the identification set; the 2 intact (un-notched) controls are a separate control set. split_independence=physical_independent (held-out specimens are physically distinct specimens, not a temporal/spatial slice of an identification specimen). The held-out set spans all three bedding orientations and all three notch depths, so the Mode III fracture-resistance anisotropy A_III can be recomputed ENTIRELY from held-out data (K4 anti-circularity).

intact_controls.role: un-notched constraint that breaks the mu(beta)/cohesion degeneracy for K3; with no notch there is no Mode III cohesive fracture, so the control force-displacement isolates crack-face friction + machine/specimen elastic compliance independently of the notch cohesive law
intact_controls.note: wanzheng-1/2 are materialised into the identification inputs (load_displacement.csv now carries 27 ANBD + 2 un-notched controls = 29 specimens; force_all_specimens.csv carries the 2 control peak rows at a=0). They enter the K3 joint inverse as the un-notched friction/compliance constraint that separates orientation-aware mu(beta) from the cohesive scalars. Whether the control-augmented inverse achieves a UNIQUE mu(beta) separation is resolved at E3/E5 by the control-augmented inversion + synthetic-twin recovery test; if it is not unique for a named physical/data reason, the K3 pre-declared real-reason downgrade applies. The mu-independent backbone (raw/frictionless anisotropy + per-orientation K_IIIc) is the strong floor regardless.

channel_availability_notes: Force-displacement is available for all 27 ANBD specimens (identification + held-out) plus the 2 un-notched intact controls (wanzheng-1/2; 29 rows in load_displacement.csv); it is the primary data-misfit channel and, for the controls, the un-notched degeneracy-breaking constraint for K3.
Surface 3D-DIC W/CSD_W is available except for the 4 DIC-excluded cells (honored downstream via the dic_csd_cod_summary.csv 'excluded' column).

beta=0 a=6 cell: both identification specimens (0-6-1, 0-6-2) are DIC-excluded and 0-6-3 is held out, so DIC-W identification for beta=0 pools across the a=4 and a=8 cells (DIC-valid); force-displacement for the 0-6 cell is still used in identification.
Held-out W-field prediction uses the 7 DIC-valid held-out cells (all except 45-6-3, 45-8-3); held-out A_III (force-based K_IIIc) uses all 9 held-out cells.

claim_coverage.K1_K2: tau_III(delta_III; beta) + G_IIIc/peak-traction identified on the 18 identification specimens (force-displacement + DIC W/CSD_W).
claim_coverage.K3: mu(beta) + cohesive scalars jointly inverted on identification K_I*/K_III* + force-displacement, with the 2 un-notched intact controls (wanzheng-1/2) entering as the friction/compliance constraint that breaks the mu/cohesion degeneracy; held-out check on ANOVA-independent replicate cells. The mu-independent backbone is the strong floor; the orientation-aware mu(beta) separation is the conditional-positive result resolved at E3/E5.
claim_coverage.K4: held-out 9 specimens (NOT used in identification) test A_III=3.62 reproduction + AE shear-fraction trend; non-circular by construction.

alternatives_considered: Replicate-holdout (chosen): held-out r3 spans all beta -> A_III recomputable from held-out alone; preserves 2 identification replicates per cell. Notch-depth-holdout (rejected as primary): hold a whole a-cell; tests notch-depth generalization but A_III would be available at one notch depth only. The claim contract K4 admits replicate OR notch-depth holdout; replicate-holdout chosen for full-orientation A_III coverage. This split is the locked-claim implementation of P2 'held-out replicate / notch-depth cell NOT used in identification' + 'physical_independent'; it can be amended at E2/E4 through a claim_pressure / repair packet if the synthetic-twin harness reveals an identifiability constraint.
